evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: Rep never framed the 10–15 minute timeboxed ask or the 'quote you can depend on' promise, and never waited for a yes before moving into probing.
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Rep asked 'do you have any questions or concerns you would like answered on this call besides pricing?' but this came after verifying contact info, not framed as an open discovery of their priorities.
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: Customer raised 'minimal furniture' and containers as the scope; rep acknowledged but moved directly into itemization (sofa, love seat, bed, etc.) without asking 'tell me more about that' or understanding the underlying concern.
evidence_quotes.active_listening_reflection: No reflection back of customer's concerns. Rep moved straight into logistics probing.
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: Rep gave a range ($720–$924 for 2.5–3.5 hours) and mentioned typical move durations, but did not personalize to this customer's specific situation (minimal items, self-moving most goods, trip fee context).
evidence_quotes.pricing_framing: Rep explained the 2.5-hour minimum and 15-minute increments, and disclosed the $210 trip fee before pricing, but never stated the 'not a guess' framing or provided upfront clarity on the full fee structure before anchoring.
evidence_quotes.feels_fair_then_silence: Rep never asked 'does that feel fair?' or any version of it. After pricing, rep immediately pivoted to truck availability.
evidence_quotes.on_time_guarantee_delivered: Rep stated: 'we value your time. So, we can't make it in the time window that we arrange. We immediately start DICOM money of your final bill' — covers discount terms, though delivery is slightly garbled.
evidence_quotes.damage_coverage_delivered: Rep stated: 'We do have our no worries damage coverage, free evaluation coverage included in the hourly rate provides up to $2,000 per move to repair, replace or reimburse for accidental damages that is on top of the state mandated 60¢ per pound coverage' — covers $2,000, no deductible framing, and that it's built in.
evidence_quotes.closes_the_loop: Rep does not ask 'does that put those to rest?' or any confirmation that the Two Promises addressed the customer's concerns.
evidence_quotes.final_concerns_check: Rep never asked 'what's still concerning you about this move?' or any genuine final concerns check before the close.
evidence_quotes.catch_all_asked: Rep never asked 'anything coming with you we haven't talked about?'
evidence_quotes.explicit_ask: Rep said 'Did you want me to go ahead and secure that for you and then if you need to, you can call us and give it cancel' — this is softened with an easy out (call us back, check with your wife first).
evidence_quotes.rate_lock_mentioned: Rep stated 'there is no deposit to get on our schedule and there's no changes or I keep saying that stay charges or fees for canceling or if you wanted to change the date' — addresses no-deposit, though does not explicitly say 'rate lock.'
evidence_quotes.booking_confirmed: Rep confirmed date (October 3rd), arrival window (8:30–9:00 AM), truck size (26 ft box truck), crew (2 movers + 1 truck), and unit number (323). Did NOT confirm phone number or address for the destination, and did NOT leave notes about customer's concerns for the crew.

top_strength: Rep clearly disclosed all fees (trip fee, hourly rate, minimum, increment structure) upfront before pricing, and successfully covered both Two Promises (On-Time Guarantee and Damage Coverage) with full detail and confidence.
coaching_note: The call skipped the foundational quid-pro-quo frame (no time-boxed ask or quote-you-can-depend-on promise) and never asked the customer's agenda before diving into logistics, which means the rep was gathering details without understanding what the customer actually cared about; go back and ask 'Other than price, what are your biggest concerns about this move?' before you start probing.
